body.statement: For all \(K,O\in\mathfrak G_p\) satisfying \(d_K=d_O\), if every \(\Gamma_i(K,O)\) and every \(\Gamma_i(O,K)\) has a perfect matching, then \(\operatorname{SCC}(K)=\operatorname{SCC}(O)\). Equivalently, if \(\operatorname{SCC}(K)\ne\operatorname{SCC}(O)\), then some graph order and vertex has \(\Delta_i>0\).
body.justification: H-star is the sole global combinatorial bottleneck and the proposal's theorem-level kernel.
body.gap: Theorem 4.13 of Drton, Hollering, and Wu proves the corresponding existence statement only when one graph is acyclic; no all-feedback proof or counterexample was found.
body.consumer: Together with Theorems 1 and 2, H-star makes every SCC-discordant equal-outdegree pair generically distinguishable by a computable precision coordinate set.

obligation.what_is_open: The universal implication from two-sided local perfect matchings to equality of the global strongly connected component partitions remains unproved for multiple changed tails.
obligation.obstruction: A matched replacement path may itself use changed edges. Every noninitial dependency descends along an edge of the certificate graph, but the first changed edge can have the comparator-only matched child as its tail. A dependency cycle can therefore mix edges from the two graphs, and neither graph's condensation order supplies a strict potential around that cycle.
obligation.attempted: Direct path substitution proves the one-tail case; a one-emitter chase proves the maximum-outdegree-one case. Condensation-order potentials and dependency-cycle induction fail at the exceptional first edge, and the supplied finite searches are evidence rather than a generic-class certificate.
obligation.partial_result: The exact closure--matching identity is proved for every ordered pair and vertex.  Moreover, two-sided perfect matchings imply \(\operatorname{Rch}(K)=\operatorname{Rch}(O)\) when only one outgoing row differs, and distinct equal-degree graphs with maximum outdegree at most one always have a positive Hall deficiency in one order.  For a general supporting dependency path \(a=x_0\to\cdots\to x_r=b\), the reversed \(K\)-path is \(b=x_r\to\cdots\to x_0=a\); every tail \(x_s\) with \(s<r\) after the first reversed edge is a \(K\)-child of the original tail \(i\).  Thus every dependency on a changed edge except possibly the first edge of that reversed path descends along a \(K\)-edge from \(i\); the exceptional first edge has tail \(b\), for which only the changed \(O\)-edge \(i\to b\) is known.
